chapter: Carey band, jazz and drum demonstrations
title: Jack Carey's six-piece band and its personnel
summary: Advertising jobs, Carey's band versus Punch's later band, and the six players including Walter Robichaux on clarinet; six pieces outdid a twelve-piece band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, when you say you played with punch band, did you ever, did you play, uh, advertising jobs on the drum?
Advertising job, yeah. Well, all, all jobs are just advertising, especially the color dancers.
Was Jack Carey then, uh, with that same band or not?
Same band.
He was with that band?
He was with the band.
But it was Punchy's band or Jack's band?
No, it was Jack Carey's band.
Jack Carey's band. Yeah.
Uh-huh. And in the later years, well, Punch pulled out from Jack and made his own band.
Well, who else was in that band besides you and Punch and Jack Carey?
Jack Carey was on trombone, myself on drum, Kid Punch on trumpet, Robichaud playing clarinet, Lorenzo Stahl playing banjo, and Lichester Siles playing baseball. It was six pieces.
You say Robichaud on clarinet? Yeah. Which Robichaud was that?
Uh, Walter Robichaud.
Walter Robichaud. Uh-huh.
Uh-huh.
Uh-huh. That sounded like a good band, wasn't it?

Yeah. Well, we were using six pieces. Uh-huh. That was a big band at the time. Uh-huh. We'd take six pieces, they're much more than what they did with a 12-piece band. Uh-huh. Because man was very powerful at the time, and everybody on his own bottom. You see what I mean?
Everybody on his own bottom, right?
Yeah. What does that mean now? Well, every man for his self.
Yeah.
